q.description: Parameter defines the search query. You can use anything that you would use in a regular Barnes & Noble search: a title, an author, a keyword, or an ISBN (e.g., `agatha christie`, `The Hobbit`, or `9780441013593`).

sort_by.description: Parameter defines the sorting order of the results. It defaults to Top Matches, the most relevant results first. Available options: `bestsellers` - Bestsellers `newest` - Newest to Oldest `oldest` - Oldest to Newest `price_low_to_high` - Price: Low to High `price_high_to_low` - Price: High to Low `title` - Title: A to Z

availability.description: Parameter defines the availability of the products to show. Both options can be separated by `||` (e.g., `in_stock||pre_order`). Available options: `in_stock` - In stock, ships in 1-2 days `pre_order` - Pre-Order

department.description: Parameter defines the department of the products to show (e.g., `Books`, `eBooks & NOOK`, `Kids' Books`, or `Toys & Games`). The departments of a search are in `filters` of the JSON response. Multiple departments can be separated by `||`.

subject.description: Parameter defines the subject of the products to show (e.g., `Mystery & Thrillers` or `Science Fiction & Fantasy`). The subjects of a search are in `filters` of the JSON response. Multiple subjects can be separated by `||`.

product_format.description: Parameter defines the format of the products to show (e.g., `Hardcover`, `Paperback`, `eBook`, `Audiobook`, or `Vinyl LP`). The formats of a search are in `filters` of the JSON response. Multiple formats can be separated by `||` (e.g., `Hardcover||Paperback`).

age.description: Parameter defines the age range of the products to show (e.g., `0 - 2 Years`, `6 - 8 Years`, or `Teens`). The age ranges of a search are in `filters` of the JSON response. Multiple age ranges can be separated by `||`.

price.description: Parameter defines the price range of the products to show (e.g., `Under $5`, `$10 - $15`, or `Over $50`). The price ranges of a search are in `filters` of the JSON response. Multiple price ranges can be separated by `||`.

rating.description: Parameter defines the minimum average rating of the products to show, from `1` to `5` stars (e.g., `4` for products rated 4 stars and up).

language.description: Parameter defines the language of the products to show (e.g., `English` or `Spanish`). The languages of a search are in `filters` of the JSON response. Multiple languages can be separated by `||`.

color.description: Parameter defines the color of the products to show (e.g., `Black`), for products like journals and accessories. The colors of a search are in `filters` of the JSON response. Multiple colors can be separated by `||`.

next_page_token.description: Parameter defines the next page token. It is used for retrieving the next page of results. Leave it unset for the first page. Barnes & Noble returns up to 24 results per page. The next page token can be found in the SerpApi JSON response: `serpapi_pagination -> next_page_token`. It must be used with the same search parameters as the search it comes from. The token expires 15 minutes after the search it comes from. Expired tokens still work up to page 5, more slowly, as Barnes & Noble's pages are loaded again from the first one. For later pages, redo the search from its first page with no_cache set to `true`.

engine.description: Set parameter to `barnes_and_noble` to use the Barnes & Noble API engine.

no_cache.description: Parameter will force SerpApi to fetch the Barnes & Noble results even if a cached version is already present. A cache is served only if the query and all parameters are exactly the same. Cache expires after 1h. Cached searches are free, and are not counted towards your searches per month. It can be set to `false` (default) to allow results from the cache, or `true` to disallow results from the cache. no_cache and async parameters should not be used together.

async.description: Parameter defines the way you want to submit your search to SerpApi. It can be set to `false` (default) to open an HTTP connection and keep it open until you got your search results, or `true` to just submit your search to SerpApi and retrieve them later. In this case, you'll need to use our Searches Archive API to retrieve your results. async and no_cache parameters should not be used together. async should not be used on accounts with Ludicrous Speed enabled.

zero_trace.description: Enterprise only. Parameter enables ZeroTrace mode. It can be set to `false` (default) or `true`. Enable this mode to skip storing search parameters, search files, and search metadata on our servers. This may make debugging more difficult.

api_key.description: Parameter defines the SerpApi private key to use.

output.description: Parameter defines the format of the result. It can be set to `json` (default) to get a structured JSON of the results, `html` to get the raw HTML retrieved, or `md` to get a Markdown-formatted version optimized for LLMs and AI agents.

json_restrictor.description: Parameter defines the fields you want to include in the output, reducing payload size for faster response. See the JSON Restrictor documentation for more details.
